authDecision.decision: Fieldgrid owns invite/recovery/challenge/e-mail/tenant/host/audit/rate limit; no magic links; no mailed or temporary password before proof; Supabase may temporarily remain only the credential/session backend; full auth replacement is a separate program.
dependencies: RLS and Storage proof for auth.uid dependent policies
Credential challenge state model and rate limits

architectureDependencies.summary: Team assignments require participant-owned execution rows, versioned events, aggregate parent status projection, participant reports/signatures, and offline replay idempotency before team closeout can be called production-safe.

canonicalItems.title: Fieldgrid-owned auth challenge and recovery boundary
acceptanceTests: Recovery completion fails without matching challenge context.
Invite activation never mails or stores a temporary password before proof.
Existing active accounts cannot be overwritten by privileged onboarding without verified linking.
Wrong-host and cross-tenant recovery attempts emit audit and denial events.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible additive credential_challenges, invite_challenges, rate-limit and audit tables; no destructive auth user rewrite.
canonicalItems.rollback: Disable new challenge issuance and keep Supabase credential/session backend; do not delete challenge/audit rows.

canonicalItems.title: Host-bound identity, platform AAL and tenant profile resolution
acceptanceTests: Every portal action resolves identity through current host tenant.
Platform terminal guards enforce platform host and required AAL/MFA policy.
RLS helpers cannot authorize first-row personnel/customer matches across tenants.
API JWT validation enforces issuer/audience and tenant authorization separately.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible forward-only RLS helper replacement; no auth provider replacement in this phase.
canonicalItems.rollback: Keep old helper functions only as compatibility fallback until new RLS proof passes.

canonicalItems.title: Assignment and planning cross-tenant IDOR closure
acceptanceTests: Cross-tenant UUIDs are denied for assignment, round, history, capacity, reschedule, re-shift, approval and deletion paths.
Zero-parent-row updates cannot trigger tenantless recalculation or audit side effects.
Denials are audited without leaking resource existence.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: No migration expected unless DB constraints are added for child ownership.
canonicalItems.rollback: Revert action-scope predicates; no data rollback expected.

canonicalItems.title: Assignment status transition bypass removal
acceptanceTests: Generic edit cannot set terminal or finance-sensitive status.
Every transition passes through a command with allowed previous state and side-effect matrix.
Privileged override requires explicit authority, reason and audit row.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: No migration expected for command routing; possible audit reason columns later.
canonicalItems.rollback: Restore old UI/action routing only if no partial side-effect data was produced.

canonicalItems.title: Tenant-bound document and media signed URL enforcement
acceptanceTests: Corrupt current-tenant rows with foreign storage_path are denied before signing.
Personnel and customer document actions require tenant and module predicates.
Path guessing and cross-tenant object requests do not produce signed URLs.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible additive cleanup registry for legacy paths; no automatic object deletion.
canonicalItems.rollback: Keep legacy paths readable only through audited server-side compatibility branch.

canonicalItems.title: Support, sensitive access and audit isolation
acceptanceTests: Sensitive access requests require active support grants.
Tenant audit log cannot show other tenant rows.
Request-route support decisions write audit rows.
Platform ticket child references belong to the selected tenant.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Forward-only RLS/revoke hardening for support grant tables may be required.
canonicalItems.rollback: Disable sensitive access creation if grant binding is inconclusive; preserve audit rows.

canonicalItems.title: Tenant entitlement, RBAC, module and sector enforcement
acceptanceTests: Role management UI mutates tenant RBAC observed by runtime permission checks.
Module-off direct routes/actions are denied for documents, finance, tickets, reports and notifications.
Sector writes validate tenant allow-lists across customers, objects, personnel and task codes.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible migration if legacy global roles or tenant-scoped customer types must be copied.
canonicalItems.rollback: Keep platform-only legacy role management separate from tenant RBAC rollout.

canonicalItems.title: Payment intent, webhook inbox and ledger integrity
acceptanceTests: Provider calls happen only after durable local intent commit.
Duplicate payment clicks and duplicate paid webhooks are idempotent under concurrent DB tests.
Webhook fails closed for missing production secret and verifies amount/currency/tenant/customer/invoice metadata.
Manual mark-paid, partial, overpayment, refunds and collection payments reconcile through the same ledger.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Likely additive payment_intents, provider_event_inbox, ledger, allocation uniqueness and collection trigger migrations.
canonicalItems.rollback: Dual-read legacy payment state until ledger parity is proven; do not delete provider events.

canonicalItems.title: Report approval, proposal and invoice atomicity
acceptanceTests: Report approval rolls back or compensates when proposal creation fails.
Personnel report insert sets tenant_id and emits durable workflow event.
Concurrent approval/rejection/proposal attempts produce one canonical outcome.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible report tenant backfill and partial unique active invoice/proposal index.
canonicalItems.rollback: Forward-fix partial approved reports; do not downmigrate workflow rows.

canonicalItems.title: Team assignment execution participant model
acceptanceTests: A single worker cannot complete or fail a team assignment unless aggregate policy allows it.
Participant-owned reports/signatures survive offline replay and concurrency.
Parent assignment status is projected only by aggregate policy.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Add assignment_execution_participants and versioned participant events; dual-read/dual-write migration required.
canonicalItems.rollback: Keep parent status compatibility during dual-run; rollback by disabling participant writes before projection cutover.

canonicalItems.title: Interest selection, scheduling and capacity candidate contract
dependencies: team execution model if selected means executable work
acceptanceTests: Selected interest cannot trap a worker outside executable assignments.
Scheduling only succeeds when required worker count and role constraints are satisfied.
Stale capacity candidates disappear after recalculation.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible uniqueness/upsert constraints for assignment_personnel promotion.
canonicalItems.rollback: Feature-flag selection promotion if planner wording changes first.

canonicalItems.title: Domain events, recipients, preferences and transactional outbox
acceptanceTests: emitDomainEvent filters every recipient by event tenant.
Customer preferences suppress delivery when product contract says opt-out.
Ticket writes and event/audit/queue rows commit atomically or enter repairable state.
Platform notification dispatch has provider-backed delivery outcomes.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible outbox/delivery state migration and idempotency keys.
canonicalItems.rollback: Keep legacy direct sends while outbox is shadow-written and compared.

canonicalItems.title: Async worker tenant lifecycle, retry, DLQ and provider idempotency
acceptanceTests: Workers re-check tenant active status and module entitlement after claim and before delivery.
Retryable delivery failure returns retry semantics and records attempts atomically.
Final failure enters explicit DLQ or repair queue.
Outbound provider calls receive idempotency keys where supported.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible DLQ/final failure state and attempt transaction changes.
canonicalItems.rollback: Preserve queue rows and stop workers if lifecycle checks misclassify tenants.

canonicalItems.title: Zero-row, stale-row and tenant settings mutation integrity
acceptanceTests: Settings updates fail on zero rows or intentionally upsert.
SMTP secrets are encrypted and tenant-scoped; no global tenant SMTP fallback is used.
Notification audience options never include other tenant personnel/customers.
Primary contact and type/catalog writes have an explicit tenant/global contract.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Likely encrypted SMTP secret migration; possible tenant-scoped customer type migration.
canonicalItems.rollback: Retain legacy SMTP readability until encrypted secret cutover is proven.

canonicalItems.title: Availability, leave and schedule replacement atomicity
acceptanceTests: Weekly availability replacement cannot delete existing windows unless replacement insert succeeds.
Concurrent approve/reject uses expected-status predicates.
Leave and availability read settings from the current portal tenant.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible validation/uniqueness constraints for weekly windows.
canonicalItems.rollback: Keep old rows untouched on failed replacement attempts.

canonicalItems.title: Personnel offline queue scope and idempotent replay
sourceEvidence: PR #292 team execution model offline replay implications
acceptanceTests: Offline queue keys and payloads are tenant/personnel/user scoped.
Replay is refused after logout, host switch or identity change.
Duplicate extra work, report notes and inventory movements are blocked by durable mutation IDs.
Service worker rejects external absolute notification targets.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Likely additive client mutation IDs and unique constraints.
canonicalItems.rollback: Disable offline replay for affected action types if idempotency proof fails.

canonicalItems.title: Upload-first media and document orphan cleanup
acceptanceTests: DB registration failure after upload creates repairable cleanup record or deletes uploaded object.
Document delete and parent delete handle Storage failures without silently losing auditability.
No automatic business-record deletion is required for cleanup.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible additive pending_uploads/cleanup table.
canonicalItems.rollback: Stop cleanup worker and preserve registry rows for manual repair.

canonicalItems.title: Tenant lifecycle, provisioning, domain and offboarding contract
acceptanceTests: Archived tenants cannot be reactivated by generic direct action.
Lifecycle mutation and audit are transactionally coupled with affected-row proof.
Legacy tenant creation delegates to canonical provisioning or is removed.
Offboarding has retention, dependency and rollback semantics.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible additive offboarding/deletion state; no destructive tenant cleanup.
canonicalItems.rollback: Keep archived tenants terminal until explicit restore program exists.

canonicalItems.title: Customer visible workflow and quote/invoice contracts
acceptanceTests: Expired sent quotes cannot be accepted unless product policy explicitly allows extension.
Quote approval next assignment state is documented and tested.
Customer-visible invoice/payment data uses shared visibility predicates.
Synthetic notifications have persisted read/delete state or are clearly display-only.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible customer notification state or report summary fields.
canonicalItems.rollback: Keep old status labels until customer copy and backend transition agree.

canonicalItems.title: Tenant-scoped reference integrity for customer, object, personnel and qualification links
acceptanceTests: Backoffice assignment create/update rejects object/customer/tenant mismatch.
Qualification role/task-code links prove all referenced records belong to current tenant.
Extra work task-code catalog is tenant scoped.
Platform ticket child refs are ownership-validated.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: Possible composite FK/unique constraints or tenant-scoped catalog migration.
canonicalItems.rollback: Use forward-fix validators; avoid destructive recategorization of existing business records.

canonicalItems.title: Route, map and realtime side-effect observability
acceptanceTests: Every assign/unassign mutation refreshes route/map contexts or records a non-blocking warning.
Realtime invalidation failure is observable.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: No migration expected.
canonicalItems.rollback: Revert side-effect additions without changing canonical assignment rows.

canonicalItems.title: Personnel invite feedback and retry semantics
acceptanceTests: Personnel create response separates row creation from invite delivery.
Invite failure shows retry state and does not imply a password was sent.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: No migration expected unless invite status is persisted.
canonicalItems.rollback: Keep invite status as UI-only until challenge protocol persists delivery state.

canonicalItems.title: Runtime evidence program and release-gate classification
sourceEvidence: All audit PRs classify their tests as static/source-level except #292 domain policy tests and #290 source-level provider/worker reproductions.
PR #278 is candidate implementation only for runtime harness, not a completed solution.
acceptanceTests: Every critical security item has a runtime test lane, not only regex/source inspection.
Test-layer labels distinguish static, DB, RLS, API, browser and provider evidence.
Skipped critical tests fail the gate.
Candidate implementation PRs are not counted as closure until their required runtime evidence passes.
canonicalItems.migrationImpact: No product migration; possible local test fixture setup only.
canonicalItems.rollback: Remove only documentation/test harness changes; no production behavior changes.
